source_inspection.title: The Cave Beneath the Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan
source_inspection.author: Rebecca Sload
source_inspection.publisher: University of Pittsburgh Center for Comparative Archaeology

findings.subject: Sedge inclusions in Sun Pyramid cave wall closure mortar
findings.assertion: At Blockage 11 in TE28 C:East SF20, Sload reports C. Earle Smith identified sedge material with gypsum mineral replacement in a wattle-and-daub fragment examined under magnification; Drewitt also reported plant remains in mud mortar of Blockage 2 south side. Neither directly dates construction nor establishes deliberate sedge addition.
findings.locator: Sload 2020 p.91; cites Millon 1978 p.105 and Drewitt 1978 p.3
findings.evidence_type: excavation construction material, specialist identification reported secondhand
findings.source_inspected: Sload 2020 printed p.91 full original page PDF screenshot; Millon/Drewitt reports not inspected
findings.confidence: moderate on report; limited on inference

findings.subject: Sun Pyramid cave lateral probing and original vs restored wall boundaries
findings.assertion: Sload reports 1978 probing every 50 cm at three heights, with lateral depths of 1-3 m beyond modern visible faces and a maximum of 2.95 m south of Station 5. In TE28 Area C, excavation found more than 1 m behind northern stacked facing and 2 m on southern side. Some visible rock walls are ancient and some later INAH consolidation; these readings cannot establish the original cross-section throughout the cave.
findings.locator: Sload 2020 printed pp.93-95 Fig.6.12; references Altschul 1978a pp.150-158 and Sload 1978a pp.53-84
findings.evidence_type: probing measurements and excavation wall sections
findings.source_inspected: Sload p.93-94 original PDF screenshots and p.95 text; 1978 notes unexamined
findings.confidence: moderate for reported local measurements; low for reconstructed cave-wide shape

findings.subject: Worked architectural materials in Sun Pyramid cave blockages
findings.assertion: Excavation photos captioned in Sload Fig.6.8 depict an overturned stone drain in the mud-mortared interior of Blockage 12 north side and a dressed stone at the ceiling junction within Blockage 3 north side. Original location and ritual use of the worked stones remain unknown.
findings.locator: Sload 2020 printed p.92 Fig.6.8a-b, photo credit Sload 1978 © R. Millon
findings.confidence: moderate for object attribution, low for previous function

enrichments.detail: At least 17 blockage walls confirmed versus earlier 19 mapped; ~25 m occupied of ~55 m between chambers and terminus. Mud-mortared rock blockages had smooth west-face concrete continuing into adjacent west floor; concrete absent under former blockage footprints. Repeated east-to-west closure sequence is inferred. Distinguish closure architecture from disputed date and motivation.

qa.issue: 17 confirmed walls vs 19 in prior mapped account
Original sidewalls versus INAH consolidation are not distinguishable everywhere
Smith sedge identification not verified against original specialist records
